answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent to a staked bond that must answer rotating, peer-graded challenges. Forge a thousand identities and you post a thousand bonds, each signing an original proof the way a quill marks a hand no stamp can copy. Every attestation is carved onto a shared ledge no actor can quietly rewrite, and graders refract each answer through a prism of distinct reasoning, so templated clones fail verification and the attacker cost scales linearly with identities instead of collapsing to zero.
